answer: Stop sybils with a harbor, a signal, and a terrace. Each identity must dock in a harbor berth: one berth, one bond, and the berth's key is a signal pulse salted to the owner's address, so one pulse validates only one face. Berths sit on a terrace of rising deposits: the k-th identity from one funder must re-post every deposit below it, so N clones pay roughly N squared to dock. Each epoch the harbor audits one terrace step; a step holding two faces from one purse is scuttled, and every berth above it sinks. One honest sailor risks one berth; a clone fleet pays quadratic tolls for one harbor.
